inline_comments.comment: The test description `'should rank affected above modified and below warning'` contradicts both the assertion and the implementation. The assertion correctly expects `'status-value:modified'` to win from `['affected', 'modified', 'success']`, because `modified` sits at a higher index in `statusPriority` (index 4) than `affected` (index 3). The description says "affected above modified" — the exact opposite. The correct description is `'should rank modified above affected and below warning'`.

The inline comment `// priority ordering (most critical wins): error > warning > affected > modified > new` describes `new` as the least critical of the three change-detection variants. This is the opposite of the actual `statusPriority` array, which places `new` at index 5, `modified` at index 4, and `affected` at index 3 — making `new` the most critical of the three. Update the comment to `error > warning > new > modified > affected`, or reorder `statusPriority` if the intended design is that `new` should be least urgent.

`StatusIconMap` sets `'status-value:new'`, `'status-value:modified'`, and `'status-value:affected'` to `null`. This map drives the status badge rendered on individual story (leaf) nodes. As a result, stories that carry these status values will display **no status badge at all**, even though the parent component/group node will show the correct icon (via `getStatus`). This is inconsistent with how `success` and `error` behave (both show at leaf and group level) and appears to contradict the PR's stated goal of surfacing which specific stories are new or have changed content.

If hiding the icon at story level is intentional, add a comment explaining the design decision. Otherwise, populate these entries with their `getStatus`-produced icons (e.g. `<svg viewBox="0 0 14 14" ...><UseSymbol type="new" /></svg>`) so the status is visible at both levels.

The `as StatusValue` cast on `'status-value:new'` (and the same on `modified`/`affected` below) is unnecessary. All three literals are now included in the `StatusValue` union in `status-store/index.ts`, so TypeScript can infer the correct type without an explicit assertion. Remove the casts to avoid implying the type system cannot handle these values on its own.

general_comments.comment:
There is a consistent conflict between the documented priority intent and the implementation across three separate locations:

1. `statusPriority` array (`status.tsx`): orders as `…success < affected < modified < new < warning < error`, meaning `new` is **more** critical than `modified` and `affected`.
2. The `StatusesChangeDetectionPriority` story comment (`Sidebar.stories.tsx`): states the opposite — `error > warning > affected > modified > new` (new = least critical).
3. The test description `'should rank affected above modified and below warning'` (`status.test.ts`): also describes `affected` as more critical than `modified`, again the reverse of the array.

The test *assertions* are consistent with the array (they pass), but the stated design intent (comments, test names) consistently describes the opposite ordering. This means either the priority array is wrong or all the prose descriptions are wrong. Decide which ordering is correct and make code, tests, and comments agree before merging.
